verdict.summary: You can create a scoped app in the App Console and connect your own account in minutes. 'Enable additional users' lets up to 500 users connect while the app is in development status. Once 50 users have linked, you have two weeks to get production approval, or Dropbox freezes new links. Dropbox won't review the production application until you reach 50 users unless you ask for early review. It checks branding, the app's privacy policy and whether you request more access than you need.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min for setup, plus 1-2 hours to prepare the production application (icon, description of how you use the API, privacy policy)
verdict.approval_wait: None for you or up to 500 dev users. Dropbox publishes no turnaround time for production review, and you must be approved within 2 weeks of reaching 50 linked users.

steps.title: Sign in to the Dropbox App Console
steps.detail: Go to the App Console and sign in with a Dropbox account. A free account works. The account you use becomes the app owner.

steps.title: Create a scoped app
steps.detail: Click 'Create app'. Choose the access type: 'App folder' if the agent only needs its own folder, or 'Full Dropbox' if it needs all files. Then enter an app name.
gotchas: The app name can't include 'Dropbox' or other Dropbox product names, start with 'drop', or use DBX/DB/DfB.
Choose 'App folder' if you can. Dropbox checks for unnecessarily broad access when you apply for production.

steps.title: Add the Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: On the app's Settings page, go to the OAuth 2 section. Add the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config under Redirect URIs. Leave 'Allow implicit grant' off.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The URI must match exactly. Dropbox rejects any redirect_uri you haven't registered.
According to a community report, http is accepted only for localhost; use https everywhere else.

steps.title: Select scopes in the Permissions tab
steps.detail: Open the Permissions tab and check only the scopes your agent needs, for example files.metadata.read and files.content.read. Click Submit. The scopes you request through Composio must be ones you checked here.
gotchas: Composio's default scopes include write access for sharing, contacts and file requests. Remove any you don't use; otherwise Dropbox may reject the production application for asking for more access than you need.
Team scopes produce a team-linked token, and a Dropbox team admin must authorize them.

steps.title: Copy the app key and secret into Composio
steps.detail: Copy the App key and App secret from the Settings page. In Composio, create a custom auth config for the dropbox toolkit and enter the key as client_id and the secret as client_secret. Use the same scopes you checked in the Permissions tab.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start a connection through Composio and approve the consent screen with the owner account. Check that the token response includes a refresh_token, which requires token_access_type=offline on the authorize URL. Then make a test API call.
gotchas: If you see the error unknown_client_id, the app key in Composio is wrong.

steps.title: Enable additional users
steps.detail: On the app's Settings page, click 'Enable additional users'. Up to 500 Dropbox users can then link while the app stays in development.
gotchas: Count your linked users. Once 50 link, you have two weeks to get production approval before Dropbox freezes new links.

steps.title: Set branding and draft a privacy policy
steps.detail: Fill in the branding fields: app name, publisher, description, app website, and small and large icons. Draft a privacy policy that covers this specific app and states what it does and doesn't do with Dropbox data.
gotchas: The icon can't look like a Dropbox logo or include the word Dropbox.

steps.title: Draft an explanation of how the app uses the API
steps.detail: For each scope you selected, write a short explanation of which feature needs it, and for the access type you chose (App folder or Full Dropbox), explain why the app needs that level. The production form asks how the app uses the API.

steps.title: Apply for production
steps.detail: On the app's Status, click 'Apply for Production', paste in your explanation of how the app uses the API, and upload the icon. If you have fewer than 50 users and need approval sooner, fill in the 'Request early review' field. Before you submit, check that the app name is the one you want to keep.
gotchas: Once the app is in production you can't rename it in the console.

steps.title: Wait for Dropbox's decision and resubmit if denied
steps.detail: Dropbox approves or denies the application. A denial includes feedback; fix the issues and resubmit. Apply early enough that you're approved within two weeks of reaching 50 users.

scopes.effect: These are the core read scopes. They're easiest to justify, especially with 'App folder' access.
Only request these if your agent writes or moves files. Dropbox checks least privilege during production review.
These are in Composio's default set. Drop any you don't use, or the production application may be rejected for unnecessary access.
OIDC identity scopes listed in Dropbox's discovery document.

scopes.scope: Team scopes (team_info, members, groups, team_data, events)
scopes.effect: These produce a token linked to the team rather than a user, and a Dropbox team admin must authorize them.

blockers.symptom: New users can't link the app after it reaches 50 users
blockers.cause: Dropbox freezes new links if the app isn't approved for production within two weeks of reaching 50 linked users.
blockers.fix: Apply for production before you reach 50 users. Once the app is frozen, only production approval fixes it; unlinking users doesn't help.

blockers.cause: Dropbox doesn't review applications until the app has linked at least 50 users.
blockers.fix: Fill in the 'Request early review' field on the application.

blockers.cause: Common causes: branding violations (name or logo), scopes or access broader than the app needs, or a breach of the Developer Terms.
blockers.fix: Follow the feedback in the denial, remove scopes you don't need or switch to 'App folder' access, fix the name and icon, then resubmit.

blockers.cause: The redirect_uri doesn't exactly match a URI registered in the App Console.
blockers.fix: Paste the exact Composio callback URL into Redirect URIs.

blockers.cause: The app key in your Composio auth config is wrong.
blockers.fix: Copy the App key again from the app's Settings page.

blockers.cause: The per-authorization rate limit was exceeded. Dropbox doesn't publish exact limits.
blockers.fix: Wait for the time given in the Retry-After header before retrying.

composio.note: You can prototype right away on Composio's managed Dropbox app. Switch to your own app when you want your app name and logo on the Dropbox consent screen. Dropbox's developer guide also says developers using a platform that wraps the DBX Platform should have their own app key. Your own app starts in development status, and once 50 users link you have two weeks to get production approval. Trim Composio's broad default scopes to what you actually use, because Dropbox reviews for least privilege.

Clicking Create app starts a wizard that asks for the access type and app name, then gives you an app key and secret.

evidence.claim: You choose 'App folder' or 'Full Dropbox' access, and the production review checks for least privilege.

evidence.claim: Team scopes produce a team-linked token and need a team admin to authorize.
evidence.quote: When an app requests team scopes for the Business API, the resulting token is associated with the team (rather than the administrator who authorized it).

evidence.claim: New apps start in development status (owner only); 'Enable additional users' allows up to 500 users.
